text.p: Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe on Friday accused Burundi's military junta of jeopardising pending peace negotiations by executing six people convicted of involvement in ethnic violence.

In a statement, Mugabe, who is current chairman of the Organisation of African Unity, warned that the July 31 execution of three ethnic Hutus, two Tutsis and a Twa might lead to a deterioration of the security situation in the East African country.

"By carrying out the hangings, President Buyoya's government, moreover, has created a situation which does not augur well for the envisaged all-party peace talks due to take place later this month," he said.

The talks, scheduled for August 25 in Arusha, Tanzania, would be the first between the government of military leader Pierre Buyoya and the main Hutu rebel group, the National Council for the Defence of Democracy.
Mugabe said Buyoya -- who seized power in a coup a year ago -- had a responsibility to contribute towards the restoration of peace and stability in the country.

Tanzania, whose former president Julius Nyerere was named by East African states to mediate with Burundi on their demand for the restoration of constitutional rule there, last week also accused Burundi's military rulers of trying to sabotage peace efforts.
